newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Wednesday were quiet following Tuesday's heavy volume at $63.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Bids were light at $62.00 and passed by owners pricing cattle at $63.00, they said.

Sales at $63.00 on Tuesday were down $1.00 from last week and likely spurred by a combination of factors that included lower CME live cattle futures on Tuesday, outlooks for lighter packer demand next week and a need for feedlots to remain current, sources said.

"There's a feeling among feedlots of a real need to get cattle sold so they don't get in trouble, (with surplus supplies of market-ready cattle)" a Kansas source said of feedlots' need to avoid getting backed up in their marketings.
"It should be a short buy week for cattle next week," he said.
Packer demand next week was seen light because of the holiday-shortened work week, with the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.
Packer buying af fed cattle also was seen light as more contract supplies become available July 1, sources said.
